ablation_path_cache.config: no cache (every token a full walk)

counts.uncached: every token walks all 64 GGM levels; no hit or miss is counted

finding.index_path_dominates: ~99% of ingest time is the k*t_PRF term -- one sealed index token per keyword and per range prefix. This is the Exp. 1 optimisation lead the plan anticipated, and it is stated here because a decision about it belongs against this end-to-end number rather than a microbenchmark table.
finding.signing_is_not_the_bottleneck: Total cost is flat across every batch size: at B=1 one ML-DSA signature per event is ~1% of ingest, and at B=512 it is ~0%. t_sign/B is therefore negligible and the batching design is validated rather than merely assumed.

head_to_head.note: Ours seals each payload (AEAD), commits it to the MMR and signs every B events with ML-DSA-65; the baselines index only. The comparison is therefore conservative for us. ODXT+Zuo22 answers keyword and range queries separately and cannot answer a keyword AND range conjunction.

oracle_validation.composed: both halves re-validated on the composed build

keyword.sizing: capacity = the stream's distinct keywords (M12 R2): the cache never evicts

range.sizing: capacity = the stream's distinct keywords (M12 R2): the cache never evicts

range_token_breakdown.derived: counts from this pass's cache profile; per-call ns timed in-process; remainder = measured - sum
range_token_breakdown.remainder_is: maps and allocation, plus the per-event payload seal, MMR append and signature amortised over the event's tokens

head_to_head.stream_is: the operating collection y = pqcl_exp::collection_median(): every tab:exp-ingest row, the ceiling included, reads this one stream

index_growth.design_reference: design §6b′ derives 5.6x from 134/24 using the 1s timestamp and log D levels; this uses the committed 1-min default and depth+1 keywords, which nearly cancel

method.end_to_end_reason: Both pipelines run in one process over identical events. Summing primitive microbenchmarks would overstate achievable throughput by crediting an ideal pipeline nobody implemented (Nitro, CCS'25).
method.range_indexing: Measured as an increment. pqc_total_ns, classical_total_ns and plaintext_total_ns answer keyword queries only. pqc_with_range_total_ns answers keyword+range via prefix expansion; its plaintext counterpart is plaintext_ordered_total_ns, an ordered map with one entry per numeric attribute, because a plaintext system answers ranges natively and prefix expansion is a cost encryption imposes. plaintext_with_range_total_ns is a diagnostic that isolates per-token crypto cost; no ratio divides by it. Every pass records its entries, and query_class names what each timing answers.

range_ingest_across_y.note: y = the collection size, as Zuo'22 fixes it at setup; the same axis as exp7

rows.classical_note: ECDSA-P256 over the same events at the same batch size; the only difference from pqc_total_ns is the signature scheme
rows.range_indexing_note: pqc_total_ns and classical_total_ns EXCLUDE range indexing, as does the top-level plaintext_total_ns they are divided by; pqc_with_range_total_ns includes it. tab:exp1's `+ range indexing` row is incremental, so the rows above it must exclude the mechanism it names.
